$comment: The spend-based circuit breaker for the research lane (#2946, requested by Eric 2026-09-16 as a stopgap ahead of the batching/model-tier redesign). Distinct from research-dispatch-budget.json (per-tick session COUNT) and the held research-daily-budget.json (rolling session COUNT): this is keyed to actual measured total_cost_usd, because a count-based cap can still be blindsided by one anomalously expensive session. Same fail-closed doctrine as the other budget files — a missing or malformed threshold refuses to dispatch rather than defaulting to unlimited.
$why: Eric's pick on #6020 (2026-11-01T14:31Z), answering the callout 'Reply A2 to trip at $100 per 4h, $200 at surge': maxSpendUsd 100 is the line at every dial position but surge, maxSpendUsdAtSurge 200 is surge's own, and scripts/moneypenny/circuit-breaker.mjs reads the position off the work-mode dial (work-mode.json, #4153) to pick between them. Sized from the measurement behind that issue: 592 research legs across 624 workflow_dispatch runs 2026-10-12..26, a mean $1.01 imputed per session, the highest 4h total at normal $83.37 (the 4h to 2026-10-30T21:24:50Z, a backlog release after 75.8 quiet hours, which nobody would call a runaway) — so $100 trips on none of the 187 real ticks replayed and still trips on the runaway #2946 was written for (about $105 in 4h, 2026-09-17). The $15 canary that sat here from 2026-09-17 was never tested by a real reading: the breaker read $0.00 on every tick for six weeks because its pattern did not match a rendered log line (#6020), and with a correct read $15 would have tripped on 123 of those 187 ticks. total_cost_usd is the CLI's imputed API-equivalent cost under a Max subscription, not a literal charge; the first dollars-to-weekly-points reading is about $16 to $24 per point (a floor, since cloud sessions are not counted), re-measured weekly on #6020.
$mechanism: Unlike the count-based caps, this cannot be computed from local git history alone — it reads real spend from recent GitHub Actions run logs (the rendered `##[notice]cost — event=<id> usd=<n>` line each research leg writes, listed over `workflow_dispatch` runs only, 200 deep) and a durable, human-clearable state carried as a GitHub issue label (never a committed file, since this repo's research lane never pushes to main directly outside a PR — issue #915, Eric 2026-08-30). Once tripped: the label goes on trackingIssue, Eric is assigned there (the same bot assignment the fitness contracts use, so the trip reaches him), and the label STAYS until a human removes it — dispatch returns empty on every subsequent tick regardless of what the rolling window recomputes to, by design (fail-hard, not fail-slow: a self-healing rolling cap would silently reopen once the expensive burst aged out of the window, which is exactly the behavior Eric asked NOT to have).
